criteria_source: The fixture only. ANALYSIS.md computes the +70% lift as (treatment_rate / control_rate) - 1, states that its denominator is four control purchases so that moving one purchase swings the figure from +36% to +125%, and records under 'Other observations' that assignment looks clean, with the arms balanced on device mix and returning-visitor share. Of the two options the user names, the record supports the second. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is choose-metric's question asked as turn 2, after a turn 1 that asks about what to do instead of shipping: run to the sample size the effect needs, or pick a higher-frequency proxy outcome such as reaching the payment step. Only turn 2 is graded. See evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks which of two named reasons makes the +70% figure unreliable: unbalanced arms, or control having only four purchases. Passes when the answer says it is the four control purchases. Mentioning that the absolute difference is also underpowered, or the +36% to +125% swing, is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says the arms are unbalanced, when it says both are problems, or when it declines to choose. An answer that additionally notes that the arms are balanced is still passing.

A response that asks which experiment is meant, rather than reading ANALYSIS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
